answer: Give every identity an expiry date it cannot dodge. Each agent key lives ninety days, then must rotate: the old key signs the new one, the handover lands on a shared log peers audit, and any gap freezes standing until a check passes. A fake farm cannot rotate quietly: ten thousand identities mean ten thousand handovers a quarter, each needing its own device signature. Faking that scale costs $8 million in hardware and 40,000 operator hours a year, and one skipped rotation exposes the whole batch. Trust grows like a walnut trellis on onyx posts: cut one vine and the gap shows at once.
